{{Short description|Example of a Semigroup}}
{{more footnotes|date=July 2024}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''semigroup with two elements''' is a [[semigroup]] for which the [[cardinality]] of the [[underlying set]] is two. There are exactly five [[isomorphic|nonisomorphic]] semigroups having two elements:
* O<sub>2</sub>, the [[null semigroup]] of order two.
* LO<sub>2</sub>, the [[left zero semigroup]] of order two.
* RO<sub>2</sub>, the [[right zero semigroup]] of order two.
* ({0,1}, ∧) (where "∧" is the [[logical connective]] "[[Logical conjunction|and]]"), or equivalently the set {0,1} under multiplication: the only [[semilattice]] with two elements and the only non-null semigroup with [[Null semigroup#Zero element in a semigroup|zero]] of order two, also a [[monoid]], and ultimately the [[two-element Boolean algebra]]; this is also isomorphic to (Z<sub>2</sub>, ·<sub>2</sub>), the multiplicative group of {0,1} modulo 2.
* (Z<sub>2</sub>, +<sub>2</sub>) (where Z<sub>2</sub> = {0,1} and "+<sub>2</sub>" is "addition modulo 2"), or equivalently ({0,1}, ⊕) (where "⊕" is the logical connective "[[exclusive or|xor]]"), or equivalently the set {−1,1} under multiplication: the only [[group (mathematics)|group]] of order two. 
The semigroups LO<sub>2</sub> and RO<sub>2</sub> are [[antiisomorphic]]. O<sub>2</sub>, {{nowrap|({0,1}, ∧)}} and {{nowrap|(Z<sub>2</sub>, +<sub>2</sub>)}} are [[commutativity|commutative]], and LO<sub>2</sub> and RO<sub>2</sub> are noncommutative. LO<sub>2</sub>, RO<sub>2</sub> and {{nowrap|({0,1}, ∧)}} are [[band (algebra)|band]]s.

In this table:
*The semigroup {{nowrap|({0,1}, <math>\wedge</math>)}} denotes the two-element semigroup containing the [[Null semigroup#Zero element in a semigroup|zero element]] 0 and the [[unit element]] 1.  The two binary operations defined by matrices in a green background are associative and pairing either with ''A'' creates a semigroup isomorphic to the semigroup {{nowrap|({0,1}, <math>\wedge</math>)}}. Every element is [[idempotent]] in this semigroup, so it is a [[Band (mathematics)|band]]. Furthermore, it is commutative (abelian) and thus a [[semilattice]]. The [[Semilattice#Connection between the two definitions|order induced]] is a [[linear order]], and so it is in fact a [[Lattice (order)|lattice]] and it is also a [[Distributive lattice|distributive]] and [[complemented lattice]], i.e. it is actually the [[two-element Boolean algebra]].
*The two binary operations defined by matrices in a blue background are associative and pairing either with ''A'' creates a semigroup isomorphic to the [[null semigroup]] O<sub>2</sub> with two elements.
*The  binary operation defined by the matrix in an orange background is associative and pairing it with ''A'' creates a semigroup. This is the [[Null semigroup#Left zero semigroup|left zero semigroup]] LO<sub>2</sub>. It is not commutative.
*The binary operation defined by the matrix in a purple background is associative and pairing it with ''A'' creates a semigroup. This is the [[Null semigroup#Right zero semigroup|right zero semigroup]] RO<sub>2</sub>. It is also not commutative.
*The two binary operations defined by matrices in a red background are associative and pairing either with ''A'' creates a semigroup isomorphic to the [[group (mathematics)|group]] {{nowrap|(Z<sub>2</sub>, +<sub>2</sub>)}}.
*The remaining eight [[binary operation]]s defined by matrices in a white background are not [[associative]] and hence none of them create a semigroup when paired with ''A''.

== The two-element semigroup ({0,1}, ∧) ==
The [[Cayley table]] for the semigroup ({0,1}, <math>\wedge</math>) is given below:
{| class="wikitable" style="margin:1em auto;"
|-
!&nbsp;<math>\wedge</math>
!&nbsp;0&nbsp;
!&nbsp;1&nbsp;
|-
|&nbsp; '''0'''&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 0&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 0&nbsp;
|-
|&nbsp; '''1'''&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 0&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 1&nbsp;
|}
This is the simplest non-trivial example of a semigroup that is not a group. This semigroup has an identity element, 1, making it a [[monoid]]. It is also commutative. It is not a group because the element 0 does not have an inverse, and is not even a cancellative semigroup because we cannot cancel the 0 in the equation 1·0 = 0·0.

This semigroup arises in various contexts. For instance, if we choose 1 to be the [[truth value]] "[[Truth|true]]" and 0 to be the [[truth value]] "[[False (logic)|false]]" and the operation to be the [[logical connective]] "[[Logical conjunction|and]]", we obtain this semigroup in [[logic]]. It is isomorphic to the monoid {0,1} under multiplication. It is also isomorphic to the semigroup
:<math> 
S = \left\{
\begin{pmatrix}
  1 & 0 \\
  0 & 1 
\end{pmatrix}, 
\begin{pmatrix}
  1 & 0 \\
  0 & 0 
\end{pmatrix}
\right\}
</math>
under [[matrix multiplication]].

== The two-element semigroup (Z<sub>2</sub>, +<sub>2</sub>) ==
The [[Cayley table]] for the semigroup {{nowrap|(Z<sub>2</sub>, +<sub>2</sub>)}} is given below:
{| class="wikitable" style="margin:1em auto;"
|-
!+<sub>2</sub>
!&nbsp;0&nbsp;
!&nbsp;1&nbsp;
|-
|&nbsp; '''0'''&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 0&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 1&nbsp;
|-
|&nbsp; '''1'''&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 1&nbsp;
|&nbsp; 0&nbsp;
|}

This group is isomorphic to the [[cyclic group]] Z<sub>2</sub> and the [[symmetric group]] S<sub>2</sub>.

== Semigroups of order 3 ==
{{main|Semigroup with three elements}}
Let ''A'' be the three-element set {{nowrap|{{mset|1, 2, 3}}}}. Altogether, a total of 3<sup>9</sup> = 19683 different binary operations can be defined on ''A''. 113 of the 19683 binary operations determine 24 nonisomorphic semigroups, or 18 non-equivalent semigroups (with equivalence being isomorphism or anti-isomorphism). 
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Friðrik Diego|author2=Kristín Halla Jónsdóttir |title=Associative Operations on a Three-Element Set|journal=The Montana Mathematics Enthusiast|date=July 2008|volume=5|issue=2 & 3|pages=257–268|doi=10.54870/1551-3440.1106 |s2cid=118704099 |url=http://www.math.umt.edu/tmme/vol5no2and3/TMME_vol5nos2and3_a8_pp.257_268.pdf|accessdate=6 February 2014}}</ref> With the exception of the [[cyclic group|group with three elements]], each of these has one (or more) of the above two-element semigroups as subsemigroups.<ref name=distler>Andreas Distler, [http://bcc2009.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Theses/andreasDthesis.pdf Classification and enumeration of finite semigroups] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402121217/http://bcc2009.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Theses/andreasDthesis.pdf |date=2 April 2015 }}, PhD thesis, [[University of St. Andrews]]</ref> For example, the set {{nowrap|{{mset|−1, 0, 1}}}} under multiplication is a semigroup of order 3, and contains both {{nowrap|{{mset|0, 1}}}} and {{nowrap|{{mset|−1, 1}}}} as subsemigroups.

== Finite semigroups of higher orders ==
Algorithms and computer programs have been developed for determining nonisomorphic finite semigroups of a given order. These have been applied to determine the nonisomorphic semigroups of small order.<ref name=distler/><ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Crvenković | first1 = Siniša
 | last2 = Stojmenović | first2 = Ivan
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Zbornik Radova Prirodno-Matematichkog Fakulteta. Serija za Matematiku. Review of Research. Faculty of Science. Mathematics Series
 | mr = 1333549
 | pages = 221–231
 | title = An algorithm for Cayley tables of algebras
 | url = https://www.emis.de/journals/NSJOM/Papers/23_2/NSJOM_23_2_221_231.pdf
 | volume = 23
 | year = 1993}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=John A Hildebrant |title=Handbook of Finite Semigroup Programs |publisher=(Preprint) |year=2001}}[http://www.math.lsu.edu/~preprint/2001/jah2001a.pdf]</ref> The number of nonisomorphic semigroups with ''n'' elements, for ''n'' a nonnegative integer, is listed under {{OEIS2C|A027851}} in the [[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]]. {{OEIS2C|A001423}} lists the number of non-equivalent semigroups, and {{OEIS2C|A023814}} the number of associative binary operations, out of a total of ''n''<sup>''n''<sup>2</sup></sup>, determining a semigroup.
